Subject: Follow-up: search demo notes and technical asks

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier today 10it clarified a lot. A couple of targeted items our infra and product teams asked to capture so we can prepare for the deep-dive: 

- Reranker flow: we do vector recall in-house (FAISS), then call a reranker to re-score top-100 candidates. Were sensitive to tail latency for interactive search (target p95 < 600ms overall). Curious if Redwood recommends shrinking top-K before rerank or relying on batching to make reranker calls cheaper.
- SDK & auth: we currently issue short-lived access tokens (TTL 2m) and rotate refresh tokens hourly. Does RedwoodSDK handle aggressive short TTLs, or should we extend lifetimes for better stability? We also want a sample mTLS setup for Dedicated.
- Tool-calling: our enrichment pipeline requires deterministic JSON output from the model (entity buckets + confidence scores). Any examples of validator hooks or fallback behavior on schema mismatch?
- Sizing: rough numbers attached (embeddings lookup qps ~180, reranker qps ~60, median prompt 110 tokens, expected peak concurrency 95). We need three capacity options for procurement (pilot, production, enterprise).

Attached: atlas-map.pdf (MVP scope) and atlas-traffic-estimates.csv.

Can we lock a 90-minute technical deep-dive Thurs or Fri this week? Ops will want Marissa and Karthik in the call.

Thanks,
Iris Park
Head of Search, Atlas AI
(attachment: atlas-traffic-estimates.csv)

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: search demo notes and technical asks

Hi Iris 10thanks for the clear list and the attachments. We're available for a 90-minute deep-dive on Friday at 10am PT; I'll send a calendar invite. High-levels below so we can focus on the hard questions in the session.

- Reranker pattern: two common approaches: 1) shrink top-K client-side to 20-40 then rerank (best for strict tail SLAs), or 2) keep top-100 and use dedicated reranker pool with pre-warmed prefix cache and continuous batching (better for quality but needs more reserved capacity). We'll bring perf numbers for both on the call.
- Tokens & SDK: Redwood SDK supports aggressive auto-refresh. Short TTLs are OK but induce more frequent refresh API calls; we typically recommend ~5m TTL with refresh grace of 30s for best tradeoff. For mTLS the Dedicated control plane supports cert rotation; Marissa will share a sample config.
- Structured output: use schema-first tool definitions + server-side validation hooks. On mismatch we recommend a strict fallback that returns a machine-readable error object to the caller rather than free-form text.
- Initial capacity guidance: given your numbers, preliminary suggestion: pilot = shared-hosted embeddings + small dedicated reranker; production = dedicated embeddings pool sized for sustained 120 qps with reranker pool concurrency cap 10; enterprise = regional dedicated clusters + predictive autoscale. We'll provide concrete node counts after reviewing your CSV.

I'll attach a calendar invite and Marissa will draft three concrete options with numbers and an ops checklist before the call.

14Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: invite.ics)

Subject: Re: Follow-up: search demo notes and technical asks  sizing proposals and config snippets attached

Hi Iris 10thanks for sending the traffic CSV. I pulled three differentiated options below (short bullets) and attached a worksheet with node math + cost delta. Full details in the deep-dive but wanted these on record so procurement can react quickly.

Option A  Pilot (low-commit):
- Embeddings: hosted shared pool; client does top-40 recall.
- Reranker: small dedicated shared reranker (2 pods), concurrency cap 12/pod, expected p95 ~800-1,000ms.
- Auth: SDK auto-refresh with 5m TTL recommended.

Option B  Production (recommended):
- Embeddings: dedicated pool sized for sustained 120 qps with continuous batching and a 10k-entry KV prefix cache for hot queries.
- Reranker: dedicated GPU-backed pool, concurrency cap 8 per GPU-pod, queue-based auto-scale trigger at 200 queue depth, 60s stabilization. Target p95 for rerank stage < 350ms.
- Autoscale: base reservation to cover 70% of median traffic, scheduled scale-ins overnight, burstable buffer for peak.
- Auth/PKI: short-lived JWTs + daily rotated refresh tokens; mTLS available for Dedicated.

Option C  Enterprise SLA:
- Regional clusters, predictive autoscale from historical telemetry, per-user rate limits and automatic fallback to lightweight reranker model under overload.
- Observability: per-request tracing and token-level cost attribution.

Sample config snippets included in the attachment: queue policy, concurrency config, and a sample SDK refresh flow. Operational reminders: asymmetric tail behavior on rerank requires lower concurrency caps; prefer GPU reranker for latency-sensitive flows.

Deliverables before the deep-dive (I'll bring these):
- Concrete node counts & concurrency caps per option (worksheet attached).
- Sample repo: SDK auth-refresh, schema validators for tool-calls, and reranker call template (link in invite).

Please confirm the 10am PT Friday deep-dive or propose an alternate slot.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: atlas-sizing-options.xlsx)
